heading: Establishment of the First Responder Network Authority

tree.heading: Establishment
tree.text: There is established as an independent authority within the NTIA the “First Responder Network Authority” or “FirstNet”.

children.heading: In general
children.text: The First Responder Network Authority shall be headed by a Board, which shall consist of—
the Secretary of Homeland Security;
the Attorney General of the United States;
the Director of the Office of Management and Budget; and
12 individuals appointed by the Secretary of Commerce in accordance with paragraph (2).

children.heading: In general
children.text: In making appointments under paragraph (1)(D), the Secretary of Commerce shall—
appoint not fewer than 3 individuals to represent the collective interests of the States, localities, tribes, and territories;
seek to ensure geographic and regional representation of the United States in such appointments;
seek to ensure rural and urban representation in such appointments; and
appoint not fewer than 3 individuals who have served as public safety professionals.

children.heading: In general
children.text: Each member appointed under paragraph (1)(D) should meet not less than 1 of the following criteria:

children.heading: Public safety experience
children.text: Knowledge and experience in the use of Federal, State, local, or tribal public safety or emergency response.

children.heading: Technical expertise
children.text: Technical expertise and fluency regarding broadband communications, including public safety communications.

children.heading: Network expertise
children.text: Expertise in building, deploying, and operating commercial telecommunications networks.

children.heading: Financial expertise
children.text: Expertise in financing and funding telecommunications networks.

children.heading: Expertise to be represented
children.text: In making appointments under paragraph (1)(D), the Secretary of Commerce shall appoint—
not fewer than 1 individual who satisfies the requirement under subclause (II) of clause (i);
not fewer than 1 individual who satisfies the requirement under subclause (III) of clause (i); and
not fewer than 1 individual who satisfies the requirement under subclause (IV) of clause (i).

children.heading: Citizenship
children.text: No individual other than a citizen of the United States may serve as a member of the Board.

children.heading: Initial appointment deadline
children.text: Members of the Board shall be appointed not later than 180 days after February 22, 2012.

children.heading: In general
children.text: Each member of the Board described in subparagraphs (A) through (C) of subsection (b)(1) shall serve as a member of the Board for the life of the First Responder Network Authority.

children.heading: Appointed individuals
children.text: The term of office of each individual appointed to be a member of the Board under subsection (b)(1)(D) shall be 3 years. No member described in this clause may serve more than 2 consecutive full 3-year terms.

children.heading: Expiration of term
children.text: Any member whose term has expired may serve until such member’s successor has taken office, or until the end of the calendar year in which such member’s term has expired, whichever is earlier.

children.heading: Appointment to fill vacancy
children.text: Any member appointed to fill a vacancy occurring prior to the expiration of the term for which that member’s predecessor was appointed shall be appointed for the remainder of the predecessor’s term.

children.heading: Staggered terms
children.text: With respect to the initial members of the Board appointed under subsection (b)(1)(D)—
4 members shall serve for a term of 3 years;
4 members shall serve for a term of 2 years; and
4 members shall serve for a term of 1 year.

children.heading: Vacancies
children.text: A vacancy in the membership of the Board shall not affect the Board’s powers, and shall be filled in the same manner as the original member was appointed.

children.heading: Selection
children.text: The Secretary of Commerce shall select, from among the members of the Board appointed under subsection (b)(1)(D), an individual to serve for a 2-year term as Chair of the Board.

children.heading: Consecutive terms
children.text: An individual may not serve for more than 2 consecutive terms as Chair of the Board.

children.heading: Frequency
children.text: The Board shall meet—
at the call of the Chair; and
not less frequently than once each quarter.

children.heading: Transparency
children.text: Meetings of the Board, including any committee of the Board, shall be open to the public. The Board may, by majority vote, close any such meeting only for the time necessary to preserve the confidentiality of commercial or financial information that is privileged or confidential, to discuss personnel matters, or to discuss legal matters affecting the First Responder Network Authority, including pending or potential litigation.

tree.heading: Quorum
tree.text: Eight members of the Board shall constitute a quorum, including at least 6 of the members appointed under subsection (b)(1)(D).

children.heading: In general
children.text: The members of the Board appointed under subsection (b)(1)(D) shall be compensated at the daily rate of basic pay for level IV of the Executive Schedule for each day during which such members are engaged in performing a function of the Board.

children.heading: Prohibition on compensation
children.text: A member of the Board appointed under subparagraphs (A) through (C) of subsection (b)(1) shall serve without additional pay, and shall not otherwise benefit, directly or indirectly, as a result of their service to the First Responder Network Authority, but shall be allowed a per diem allowance for travel expenses, at rates authorized for an employee of an agency under subchapter I of chapter 57 of title 5, while away from the home or regular place of business of the member in the performance of the duties of the First Responder Network Authority.

notes.heading: References in Text
notes.text: Level IV of the Executive Schedule, referred to in subsec. (g)(1), is set out under section 5315 of Title 5, Government Organization and Employees.
